summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale, enabling teams to trace prompts, monitor costs, detect regressions, and ensure reliability across production pipelines. The LLM observability platform market reached an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and is projected to hit $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, with Gartner predicting it will account for 50% of all GenAI deployment investments by 2028. Without proper observability, teams operate blind to token waste, latency spikes, hallucinations, and runaway API costs.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain executions, agent runs, prompt versions, and evaluation datasets across LangChain and non-LangChain workflows
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Prompt versioning and regression testing
Dataset management for evaluation
Human feedback annotation workflows
Integration with LangChain ecosystem
Latency and token usage per trace
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces; Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £80/month at 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain who need deep trace debugging, prompt management, and evaluation pipelines in a tightly integrated environment

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per request, latency, model performance, and user-level spend across providers
features: One-line proxy setup with minimal configuration
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and prompt threat detection
User-level cost attribution
Open-source and self-hostable
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month with compliance features; Enterprise custom. Approximately £20/month at 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing cost visibility and quick setup who need a gateway-based proxy solution with strong spend optimization across multiple LLM providers

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, evaluation runs, model experiments, dataset versions, prompt iterations, and production inference quality
features: Experiment tracking and model versioning inherited from W&B core
LLM call tracing and span visualization via Weave
Evaluation framework with custom scoring functions
Dataset and artifact lineage tracking
Collaborative dashboards for team reporting
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team plans start at $50/month per seat; Enterprise pricing custom. Consumption-based components for compute and storage apply at scale.
tools.best_for: ML-heavy teams who already use W&B for experiment tracking and want to extend observability seamlessly into LLM evaluation and production monitoring without adopting a new platform

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, retrieval quality, hallucination signals, model drift, agent spans, and enterprise-scale telemetry
features: OpenTelemetry-native tracing for LLMs and agents
Embedding visualization and clustering for RAG debugging
Online and offline evaluation with LLM-as-judge
Drift detection and data quality monitoring
Arize Phoenix open-source version for local use
Enterprise connectors for existing ML monitoring pipelines
Long-standing ML monitoring extended to LLM workflows
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host (source-available license). Arize cloud platform offers a free tier; Growth and Enterprise plans are custom-priced based on volume and features.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing production-grade telemetry, RAG pipeline debugging, and embedding-level insights with a mature ML observability foundation

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, evaluation scores, token costs, latency, user sessions, and agent multi-step runs
features: Open-source with full self-hosting support
Detailed prompt management and versioning
Manual and automated evaluation scoring
Session and user-level trace grouping
Native SDKs for Python, JS/TS, and OpenAI integration
Cost tracking across multiple model providers
Active open-source community and frequent releases
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud tiers from approximately £20/month for 500K requests. Self-hosted is free with infrastructure costs around £30/month and ~2 hours/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams and startups wanting full control over their observability data with strong prompt management, tracing, and evaluation without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, spans, traces, and token usage via OpenTelemetry instrumentation across frameworks and providers
features: OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation for LLM calls
Framework-agnostic tracing compatible with any OTEL backend
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, and others
Exports to Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, and other OTEL-compatible backends
Open-source and vendor-neutral
Low overhead span collection with standard semantic conventions
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Backend costs depend on your chosen OTEL-compatible observability platform (e.g., Grafana Cloud, Datadog, self-hosted Jaeger).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with existing OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM observability without adopting a new proprietary platform, keeping full flexibility over their telemetry backend

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM response quality, evaluation metrics, hallucination rates, RAG retrieval scores, safety violations, and regression across prompt changes
features: 50+ research-backed evaluation metrics via DeepEval open-source library
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft for LLM evaluation
Online evaluations integrated directly into the observability layer
RAG-specific metrics including faithfulness and contextual relevance
CI/CD integration for automated regression testing on every deployment
Safety and red-teaming evaluation support
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source library is free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier; paid plans vary by evaluation volume and team size. Contact for enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing evaluation depth and quality assurance who want the richest set of automated LLM metrics integrated into both development workflows and production monitoring

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt logs, infrastructure metrics, application logs, frontend RUM, and full DevOps telemetry in a unified platform
features: Unified LLM observability plus full infrastructure monitoring in one deployment
Logs, metrics, traces, and real user monitoring (RUM) combined
Eliminates need for a separate DevOps telemetry stack
OpenTelemetry compatible ingestion
Cost-efficient storage with columnar compression
Open-source with self-hosting option
Dashboards for prompt tracing and cost tracking alongside infra metrics
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host. Cloud managed tiers available with consumption-based pricing. Significantly lower storage costs than Datadog or Elastic at scale.
tools.best_for: Full-stack teams tired of managing separate LLM observability and DevOps monitoring stacks who want a single unified platform covering both application and infrastructure telemetry

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical requests return cached responses rather than burning tokens, which can cut repeat-query costs by 40-70% in high-traffic applications.

Right-size your model selection by use case: use smaller, cheaper models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku) for classification, routing, and simple extraction tasks, reserving frontier models only for complex reasoning — observability traces from LangSmith or Langfuse make it easy to identify which calls genuinely require premium models.

Set token budget limits and monitor per-user and per-feature spend: use observability tools to attribute costs at the user, session, or feature level so you can identify runaway consumers, enforce soft limits, and prioritize optimization efforts where spend is highest rather than optimizing blindly.

Continuously evaluate and shorten system prompts: bloated system prompts silently inflate every single API call — use evaluation frameworks like DeepEval or Langfuse scoring to run A/B tests on shorter prompt variants, ensuring quality is maintained while reducing input token counts across millions of requests.
